title: Internal Hom complex from a sheaf in degree zero
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme, $P$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules, and $K^\bullet$ an arbitrary (possibly unbounded) cochain complex of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules. Let $P[0]$ be the complex concentrated in degree zero and let $T_P=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_Y}(P,-)$ be ordinary internal sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. There is an isomorphism of cochain complexes between $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P[0],K^\bullet)$ [def-pur-hom-complex] and degreewise application of $T_P$ to $K^\bullet$. No local freeness or exactness assumption on $P$ is needed. Postcomposition makes $T_P$ additive.

source.place: Section 0A8X, section-hom-complexes: product terms and differential, specialized to a source in degree zero

proof.text: In each degree n, all product factors Hom(P[0]^p,K^(p+n)) with p nonzero are zero, since P[0]^p is zero. This is also the image of a zero object under the additive contravariant sheaf Hom functor. The product universal property identifies the product with its sole surviving factor at p=0, Hom(P,K^n). Its inverse is the product lift with identity in that factor and zero in the others. Both inverse identities follow by composing with all product projections.

Project the defining differential formula to the surviving factor. The source differential of P[0] is zero, so its precomposition term vanishes by additivity of contravariant sheaf Hom. The remaining term is postcomposition with the coefficient differential. Hence the degreewise isomorphisms are an isomorphism of cochain complexes, by HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents.

Postcomposition of localized linear maps is additive sectionwise. This proves the additive instance for ordinary sheaf Hom used to form its degreewise complex functor. The preceding two steps therefore give the claimed isomorphism for every coefficient complex; no naturality theorem is required by the parent proof.
